title: AI Safety and Permission Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Capability limits, access controls, sandbox policies, and audit requirements for AI systems. The AI Safety and Permission Database is the rulebook that keeps powerful AI systems inside their bounds: what an AI may do, what needs approval, what is forbidden, and how every action is audited. Records include permission-tier definitions, sandbox policies, capability-limit specifications, audit-log schemas, and incident patterns with the control that would have stopped them. Safety here is engineering, not slogans — every rule is testable.

title: AI Safety and Permission Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Permission model: default-deny; every capability needs an explicit grant. Tiers: T0 observe-only, T1 read-scoped, T2 write-scoped with logging, T3 sensitive with human approval, T4 forbidden. Sandbox: filesystem jail (allowed roots), network egress allowlist, process limits (no fork bombs), secret isolation (credentials never in model context). Refusal engineering: refuse plainly, state the rule class, offer the safe alternative; never lecture. Audit: append-only log of (timestamp, actor, action, target, policy-decision, result); logs are tamper-evident (hash-chained). Incident taxonomy: permission creep, prompt injection via tool results, confused deputy, over-delegation. Each incident record names the missing or failed control.

title: AI Safety and Permission Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: default-deny test (unlisted actions are denied); tier test (each tier behaves per spec); audit test (every action in a test run appears in the log); tamper test (modified logs fail verification); refusal test (forbidden capabilities are refused, not attempted). Limitations: policies cannot cover unknown capabilities; hosts must actually enforce; audit logs need secure storage. Policies carry version numbers and review dates.

demo.title: Verification: calibration error (ECE)
demo.code: const pairs=[[0.9,1],[0.9,1],[0.9,0],[0.6,1],[0.6,0],[0.6,0]];const bins={};pairs.forEach(([c,ok])=>{const b=Math.round(c*10)/10;(bins[b]=bins[b]||{n:0,c:0,conf:0});bins[b].n++;bins[b].c+=ok;bins[b].conf+=c;});let ece=0;for(const b in bins){const B=bins[b];ece+=Math.abs(B.c/B.n-B.conf/B.n)*(B.n/pairs.length);}J({ece:+ece.toFixed(3)});assert(ece>0&&ece<1,'ece');
